title: Enhance Streamlit's Compatibility with Playwright on Windows by Updating Event Loop Configuration
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit's use of the older Selector event loop on Windows conflicts with Playwright's need for the newer Proactor event loop. This incompatibility causes exceptions when using Playwright for web scraping within Streamlit. The same issue will affect any other modules relying on the Proactor event loop in addition to Playwright.


### Why?

Playwright requires the Proactor event loop on Windows to run its driver in a subprocess, as the Selector event loop does not support async subprocesses. The Proactor event loop has replaced the Selector event loop as the default event loop on Windows starting with Python 3.8. The issue is [documented](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/library#incompatible-with-selectoreventloop-of-asyncio-on-windows) in Playwright's official documentation.


### How?

Proposing a modification or removal of the `_fix_tornado_crash` function in Streamlit ([source code](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/e4ab8f4578eac6c8b5ca4d518bf65f09849ea2b2/lib/streamlit/web/bootstrap.py#L406)). This function currently enforces the Selector event loop, which is incompatible with Playwright. An alternative solution could be introducing a configurable option for users to select the appropriate event loop.


### Additional Context

Tornado 6.1, released on October 30, 2020, supports the Proactor event loop on Windows (source: [Tornado 6.1 Release Notes](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/releases/v6.1.0.html)). Additionally, a related discussion in the Bokeh GitHub repository ([issue #12018](https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh/issues/12018)) and the [subsequent PR](https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh/pull/12019) supports the feasibility of this update.
